criteria_source: The fixture only. routes/orders.js posts an INSERT into orders with no deduplication of any kind, and db.js's own comment states that every write goes through write() and that it is the one place a transaction begins. The criterion is what those two files make available, not anything in rules/laconic.md. This case asks five design turns and only the last is graded. The four before it - account scoping, the unread deleted_at column, what write() does when the pool drops, and request logging - are chosen to be answerable from the same files and to touch nothing the trap grades, so the final question stays fresh and what varies is how much of its own prior output the model carries. Built for #113: its measurement is the closing-offer rate per turn, which needs no judging.
trap:
Passes when the answer keys the retry on a value the client supplies and the database enforces - an idempotency key column on orders carrying a unique constraint, so a replayed POST returns the row the first attempt created instead of inserting a second one. Naming db.write() as the single place that enforcement belongs is correct and is a bonus rather than a requirement, since the fixture's own comment says every write goes through it. Fails when the answer deduplicates on the request body alone without a client-supplied key, since two genuine orders for the same sku and quantity are indistinguishable from a retry; when it proposes only application-side checking with no unique constraint, which races under the concurrent retries idempotency exists for; when it generates the key server-side per request, which defeats the mechanism because a retry produces a new one; or when it treats this as a client responsibility and specifies nothing on the service.

A response that asks which framework or which database is meant, rather than reading the fixture, is NOT EXERCISED.
